description: We’re Ayesha , Faria and Humema from Karachi,teammates since the NYLP AI Hackathon which we won 3rd place all over the world.We build AI agents and web apps with Next.js and Python. For the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge,we’re making a 3D browser game where students run Moon and Mars outposts, balancing oxygen, power, food and radiation to keep their crew alive.Real NASA data drives every choice, and an AI Mission Control explains why missions succeed or fail.
summary: First Footprints is a 3D browser game that trains kids aged 8 to 14 like real NASA astronauts. Players pick a world on a 3D solar system built from NASA planet maps and the Tycho star map. On Earth they go through a six-level Astronaut Academy based on real NASA procedures: suiting up in the real NASA spacewalk suit and pressurizing it to 4.3 psi, a buddy check, tether discipline, handrail translation, sample protocol and an EVA course. Then they land on the Moon and keep an outpost alive in Gale Crater on Mars. ODDYSSEY, an AI guide, explains why every step matters, explains why a wrong choice is dangerous, and gives hints when a player is stuck. Instead of quizzes, kids learn by doing the procedures in the right order. It runs in any browser with no install, so any school can use it.
details: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Three.js on the frontend, and an Express and TypeScript backend. ODDYSSEY uses Google Gemini and falls back to built-in answers when offline. The game math is plain code, so the AI never changes scores or resources. Mars messages have a real 12.5 light-minute delay. The team looked at real NASA training order, kid-friendly language, low-end school computers, and keyboard and touch controls.
dataRefs: Mars Science Laboratory, Curiosity at Gale Crater
